question: The total replenishable groundwater resource in the country is about 432 cubic km. Accordingly, which water body has 26.55% of the total replenishable groundwater resource?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmaputra:**

 
 
• The Brahmaputra basin has a significantly high percentage of India's replenishable groundwater resources.
 
• This is largely due to the heavy rainfall in the region and the river's large catchment area.
 
• The basin covers parts of northeastern India and is known for its extensive alluvial aquifers.
 
• The high rainfall and flood plain areas contribute to ground water recharge.
 
• The Brahmaputra river and its tributaries plays a very important role in this region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahanadi:**

 
 
• The Mahanadi basin is located in central India and covers parts of Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
 
• While it has groundwater resources, they are significantly less than the Brahmaputra basin.
 
• The basin is affected by seasonal variations in rainfall, which impacts groundwater recharge.
 
• The Mahanadi river is very important for agriculture in the region.
 
• The region has a mix of geological formations.
 
 
 
• **Kaveri:**
 
 
• The Kaveri basin is located in southern India and covers parts of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is a water-stressed region, with limited groundwater resources.
 
• The basin is heavily reliant on rainfall and surface water for irrigation and domestic use.
 
• The Kaveri River has been a source of dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
 
• The region has a large population, that depends on the water resources.
 
 
 
• **Godavari:**
 
 
• The Godavari basin is one of the largest river basins in India, covering parts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It has moderate groundwater resources, but they are less than the Brahmaputra basin.
 
• The basin faces challenges related to groundwater depletion and water quality.
 
• The Godavari river is considered to be one of the holy rivers of India.
 
• The region has varied geological formations.
